The real and integer periodic implementations pass Mloc-style pitches and widths to cudaMemcpy2D rather than explicitly byte-scaled values. The CUDA Fortran overload contract is external; if byte units apply, the copies under-transfer multi-byte elements.

PHI_COLL_OUTER_GPU duplicates hundreds of lines of PHI_COLL_GPU reflection logic but omits its final communication call. The duplication makes later parity/boundary fixes prone to diverge and is the direct source of the internal-halo inconsistency above.

Boundary kernels write neighbor indices through expanded Ibeg-1:Iend+1/Jbeg-1:Jend+1 ranges without receiving Mloc/Nloc, so safety depends on a caller-established ghost-width contract not checked here.
